title: Gallant Conversation (Paternal Admonition)
source: Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam (public domain). Wikimedia Commons: Gerard ter Borch - Interieur met drie figuren die met elkaar in gesprek zijn; bekend als 'De vaderlijke vermaning' - Google Art Project.jpg
caption: Everyone read this painting wrong for 150 years. #arthistory #lovestory #painting #oilpainting #art
_verify: Rijksmuseum SK-A-404, about 1654; another version in Berlin (Wikipedia EN, Gallant Conversation).
Goethe described it as a father admonishing his daughter (Wikipedia EN).
A coin in the man's hand, overpainted: reported in the literature; not visible, slide says 'experts think'.
The brothel reading is the modern interpretation, not certain; slide avoids the word.

slides.headline: For 150 years, everyone read this painting wrong.
slides.sub: Gerard ter Borch, Gallant Conversation, about 1654

slides.headline: A family scene?
slides.text: A daughter in shimmering satin, a father talking, a mother sipping wine. Goethe called it a father's warning to his daughter.

slides.headline: The satin
slides.text: Look at her dress first. Ter Borch was famous for painting satin, and this silver gown is the star of the room.

slides.headline: The 'father'
slides.text: But look at the 'father' again. He is young, with a sword and a feathered hat. He looks nothing like her father.

slides.headline: His hand
slides.text: His hand is raised as he talks. Experts think it once held a coin, later painted out to make the scene look decent.

slides.headline: The 'mother'
slides.text: The older woman drinks and keeps her eyes on her glass. In paintings like this, she is not a mother but a go-between.

slides.headline: The bed
slides.text: And right behind them stands a bed with red curtains. This is not a family parlour at all, and the bed is the clue.

slides.headline: The dog
slides.text: Only the dog wanders in calmly, as if it understands what kind of room this is better than we ever did.

slides.headline: Her answer
slides.text: We never see her face. Will she accept his offer, or turn away? Ter Borch keeps her answer hidden forever.
